paragraphs: Apple CEO John Ternus is reportedly spending far more time in the design studio than Tim Cook ever did. He’s there several times a week, sometimes more than once a day.
It’s clearly different from the Tim Cook era. Many people think design influence at Apple slipped after Jony Ive left the company back in 2019, but Ternus seems determined to fix that.

John Ternus has spent virtually his entire career at Apple, joining the company’s product design team in 2001. He rose through the ranks until he reached senior vice president of hardware engineering in 2021.

That makes Ternus an unusually product-focused CEO. Before taking the top job, he spent years directly overseeing the engineers responsible for building Apple’s hardware. And that’s shaping how he runs the company since taking over as Apple CEO on September 1.
Ternus was already familiar with the space from his years running hardware engineering. Apparently, now he’s treating it like a second office.

Ternus is reportedly able to do that because other executives are handling Cook’s old turf. CFO Kevin Parekh is handling finances, while COO Sabih Khan is overseeing the supply chain. That frees up Ternus to focus on engineering and design.

Gurman says Ternus told employees he has to lead himself instead of copying Cook. Cook spent his tenure working where he could add the most value. Ternus could be wanting to do the same, but in different places.

Apple hasn’t had a true design chief since Jony Ive’s exit in 2019. Industrial design and human interface teams each had their own leaders, and they answered to former COO Jeff Williams, who retired in 2025.
